epics.title: Account and Session Management
epics.jtbd: When managing my outreach infrastructure, I want to onboard, monitor, and securely route Telegram sessions via proxies, so that I can scale my accounts without getting banned.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease account IP ban rate to <1%
requirements: R1: Ability to add new Telegram accounts via OTP or session/tdata file upload.
R2: Mandatory assignment of dedicated proxies per account.
R3: Real-time tracking of account status (Active, Spam-Block, Ban, etc.).
R4: Human behavior emulation with randomized pauses and typing signals.
R5: Daily messaging rate limiter per account.

slices.title: Account and proxy schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing data models for this epic, I want to define the schema for TG_Accounts and Proxies, so that I can scale my accounts without getting banned.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an account creation request, When the payload includes proxy details, Then it is stored in PostgreSQL.
Given a session state update, When the health monitor detects a ban, Then the DB status updates.

slices.title: Shared API contract for Account Management
slices.jtbd: When implementing the account endpoints for this epic, I want to define the OpenAPI contract, so that I can scale my accounts without getting banned.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the contract, When generating client stubs, Then the types match the account management endpoints.
Given backend implementation, When validated against contract, Then no mismatches occur.

slices.title: Account session and proxy onboarding API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the onboarding API for this epic, I want to provide REST endpoints for OTP and session file uploads, so that I can scale my accounts without getting banned.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an invalid proxy, When adding an account, Then the API rejects the request.
Given a valid OTP or session file, When submitted, Then the API registers the account and binds the proxy.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 errors during session parsing and OTP flow

slices.title: Account management dashboard
slices.jtbd: When implementing the frontend for this epic, I want to build a Svelte UI for onboarding and monitoring accounts, so that I can scale my accounts without getting banned.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the dashboard, When viewing accounts, Then their health statuses are displayed.
Given the add account form, When uploading a tdata file, Then the UI shows a progress indicator.

slices.title: Session behavioral and rate limit engine
slices.jtbd: When implementing the behavioral engine for this epic, I want to enforce daily limits and randomized pauses, so that I can scale my accounts without getting banned.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an outgoing message, When dispatched, Then a randomized pause and typing signal precedes it.
Given the daily limit is reached, When attempting to send, Then the system blocks the action.

epics.title: Cold Outreach and Campaign Management
epics.jtbd: When running lead generation campaigns, I want to ingest leads, generate spintax/LLM offers, and rotate accounts, so that I can dispatch personalized messages at scale continuously.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Increase campaign delivery success rate to >95%
requirements: R1: Import lead target lists via CSV, TXT, or manual batch entry.
R2: Dynamic text randomization using Spintax syntax.
R3: Use LLM to dynamically rephrase outreach offers based on lead profile metadata.
R4: Dynamic failover to rotate accounts upon reaching daily limits or FLOOD_WAIT errors.

slices.title: Campaign and Lead Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing the schema for this epic, I want to define tables for Campaigns and Leads, so that I can dispatch personalized messages at scale continuously.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a campaign config, When saved, Then spintax rules are stored in Postgres.
Given a lead import, When processed, Then contacts are saved in the Leads table.

slices.title: Shared API contract for Campaigns
slices.jtbd: When implementing campaigns for this epic, I want to define the REST API for creating campaigns and importing leads, so that I can dispatch personalized messages at scale continuously.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API contract, When reviewed, Then endpoints for lead upload and campaign creation are fully documented.
Given the contract, When used, Then both frontend and backend validate successfully against it.

slices.title: Campaign builder and Lead import UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the campaign UI for this epic, I want to build a Svelte view for creating campaigns and uploading CSV lists, so that I can dispatch personalized messages at scale continuously.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the campaign view, When uploading a CSV, Then the UI shows parsing progress and valid rows.
Given the spintax editor, When typing, Then it highlights spintax syntax.

slices.title: Campaign management and ingestion API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the campaign API for this epic, I want to parse CSVs and manage campaign CRUD, so that I can dispatch personalized messages at scale continuously.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a CSV upload, When received, Then it parses the rows and inserts them into the database.
Given a new campaign, When saved, Then the configuration is persisted.

slices.title: Spintax and LLM personalization engine
slices.jtbd: When implementing personalization for this epic, I want to generate variations using Spintax and Spring AI, so that I can dispatch personalized messages at scale continuously.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a spintax string, When evaluated, Then a random variant is generated.
Given lead metadata, When evaluated via LLM, Then a personalized rephrased offer is returned.

slices.title: Account rotation and failover logic
slices.jtbd: When implementing dispatch logic for this epic, I want to detect FLOOD_WAIT and limit errors to automatically failover, so that I can dispatch personalized messages at scale continuously.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an account hitting a limit, When a send is attempted, Then the job reassigns to the next available account.
Given a FLOOD_WAIT error from Telegram, When caught, Then the account is marked temporarily blocked and rotation occurs.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% success rate of failovers on FLOOD_WAIT

epics.title: AI Dialogue Engine
epics.jtbd: When a lead replies, I want the AI to process the message with full context, apply stop-triggers, and qualify the lead, so that human agents only step in when necessary.
requirements: R1: Background worker monitoring inbound responses and triggering AI evaluation.
R2: Persist conversation context (last N turns) in PostgreSQL and supply to LLM.
R3: Configurable prompt template for AI persona, goals, tone, and rules.
R4: Detect intent flags (booking, negativity) or max turns to pause AI automatically.
R5: Mark dialogue as Awaiting Human Intervention on stop-trigger and halt AI.

slices.title: Dialog and Message Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing data storage for this epic, I want to model Dialogs and Messages, so that human agents only step in when necessary.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an inbound message, When received, Then it is stored with sender type in the Messages table.
Given a dialog, When a stop-trigger fires, Then its AI state is updated in the DB.

slices.title: Inbound event listener and context builder
slices.jtbd: When implementing the event pipeline for this epic, I want to consume Telegram updates and construct the context history, so that human agents only step in when necessary.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an incoming Telegram message, When processed, Then it is persisted and the dialogue context is fetched.
Given a new turn, When history is too long, Then it truncates to the last N turns.

slices.title: Spring AI evaluator and intent detection
slices.jtbd: When implementing the LLM integration for this epic, I want to generate responses based on the system prompt and detect stop-triggers, so that human agents only step in when necessary.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a configurable persona, When responding, Then the LLM output adheres to the instructions.
Given an intent flag like a booking request, When detected, Then the AI returns an escalation signal.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: <5% false positive rate on intent detection

slices.title: Escalation and handoff controller
slices.jtbd: When implementing the workflow for this epic, I want to process AI stop-triggers to update dialog status and halt automated outreach, so that human agents only step in when necessary.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a detected stop-trigger, When processed, Then the dialogue status becomes 'Awaiting Human Intervention'.
Given a halted dialogue, When new messages arrive, Then the AI does not automatically reply.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 AI replies sent after handoff trigger

slices.title: Shared API contract for AI Configuration
slices.jtbd: When implementing the AI settings for this epic, I want to define the prompt and rule configuration API, so that human agents only step in when necessary.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the contract, When tested, Then it covers prompt updates and stop-trigger configuration.
Given frontend usage, When executed, Then it perfectly aligns with the backend.

slices.title: AI System Prompt configurator
slices.jtbd: When implementing the settings UI for this epic, I want to build a form for defining the persona, tone, and stop-rules, so that human agents only step in when necessary.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the settings view, When updating the prompt template, Then it is saved successfully.
Given the stop-triggers, When adding a new intent flag, Then it updates the configuration.

epics.title: Live Chat CRM and Human Control Panel
epics.jtbd: When managing active conversations, I want to monitor chats in a unified dashboard and take manual control when necessary, so that I can close deals that the AI has escalated.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease human response time to escalated chats to <5 mins
epics.tocConstraintRef: Live chat socket or polling latency
requirements: R1: Consolidated Svelte interface displaying incoming messages across all connected accounts.
R2: Visual status color-coding for conversations (AI Active, Human Intervention Required, Closed, Spam).
R3: Manual takeover operator override to send a manual message and immediately pause the AI.

slices.title: Shared API contract for Live Chat CRM
slices.jtbd: When implementing the CRM for this epic, I want to define WebSocket/REST APIs for real-time messaging, so that I can close deals that the AI has escalated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the contract, When used, Then endpoints for fetching conversations and sending manual messages are present.
Given real-time requirements, When documented, Then WebSocket event payloads are typed.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% interface agreement between FE and BE

slices.title: CRM unified inbox and messaging API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the inbox backend for this epic, I want to serve chat histories and handle manual dispatch requests, so that I can close deals that the AI has escalated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a request for inbox chats, When fetched, Then conversations from all accounts are returned.
Given a manual message request, When sent, Then it is dispatched via the Telegram layer.

slices.title: Manual takeover hijack logic
slices.jtbd: When implementing the override mechanism for this epic, I want to intercept manual replies to automatically flag the dialog as hijacked, so that I can close deals that the AI has escalated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an AI-active conversation, When a manual message is sent, Then the status updates to paused.
Given a paused dialogue, When a lead replies, Then the AI ignores the reply.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 race conditions when hijacking active chats

slices.title: Unified Inbox UI and Chat Window
slices.jtbd: When implementing the CRM frontend for this epic, I want to build a Svelte UI displaying the chat list with color-coding, so that I can close deals that the AI has escalated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the inbox, When an escalated chat is shown, Then it is color-coded yellow.
Given the composer, When an operator types and sends, Then the message appears in the stream.

epics.title: Anti-Ban and Account Warm-up System
epics.jtbd: When utilizing Telegram accounts, I want to automate warm-up actions and enforce aged-account rules, so that I can maximize account lifespan and trust scores.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Increase account lifespan average to >30 days
requirements: R1: Automated background actions to warm up accounts (subscribing, reading, maintaining online status).
R2: Strict account filter ensuring only 1-3 months aged accounts are assigned to outreach tasks.
R3: Calculates variable action intervals using exponential non-deterministic time distributions.

slices.title: Warm-up Configuration Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing schema for this epic, I want to track account age and warm-up state, so that I can maximize account lifespan and trust scores.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new account, When inserted, Then its creation date and warm-up status are recorded.
Given a warm-up cycle, When complete, Then the trust score updates.

slices.title: Exponential delay and age filter logic
slices.jtbd: When implementing the delay logic for this epic, I want to calculate non-linear action intervals and filter out non-aged accounts, so that I can maximize account lifespan and trust scores.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an action request, When scheduling, Then the delay is computed via an exponential distribution.
Given a campaign assignment, When choosing an account, Then it rejects accounts under 1 month old.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: <1% deviation from target exponential distribution curve

slices.title: Automated background warm-up worker
slices.jtbd: When implementing the warm-up routines for this epic, I want to execute channel subscriptions and read actions, so that I can maximize account lifespan and trust scores.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a warm-up task, When executed, Then the account subscribes to a channel and marks it as read.
Given a background schedule, When running, Then it correctly utilizes the exponential delays.
